statements.text: [[revenue|Revenue]] grew 1.9% in the year ended December 31, 2025, to $47.9 billion. This means the company sold more than the year before.
In the [[quarter|quarter]] ended April 3, 2026, revenue was $12.5 billion, up 12.1% from the same quarter a year earlier.
[[net-income|Net income]], the profit left after all costs and taxes, rose 23.3% to $13.1 billion in the year ended December 31, 2025.
After paying for the products it sold, the company kept about $62 of every $100 of sales. This is called its [[gross-margin|gross margin]].
Out of every $100 of sales, about $27 was left as profit after all costs and taxes. This is called its [[profit-margin|profit margin]].
Its day-to-day business brought in $7.4 billion of cash in the year ended December 31, 2025. This is called [[cash-from-operations|cash from operations]].
On April 3, 2026, the company had $10.6 billion in [[cash-and-equivalents|cash and cash equivalents]], money it can use quickly.
On April 3, 2026, it owed $39.1 billion in [[long-term-debt|long-term debt and lease obligations due after the next 12 months]].

figures.label: long-term debt and lease obligations due after the next 12 months

statements.text: On that date it owed more in long-term debt than it held in cash.

figures.label: long-term debt and lease obligations due after the next 12 months

statements.text: On April 3, 2026, the company had $30.4 billion in cash and other assets it expects to use within a year, against $22.4 billion of bills due within a year. That is about $1.36 for every $1 it owes soon, more than enough to cover them. This is its [[current-ratio|current ratio]].
It owned $104.2 billion in [[assets|assets]] and owed $68.5 billion in [[total-liabilities|total liabilities]], so it owned about $1.52 for every $1 it owed.

statements.text: For every $1 of [[shareholders-equity|shareholders' equity]] ($33.6 billion), it owed about $1.16 in long-term debt ($39.1 billion). This is its [[debt-to-equity|debt-to-equity ratio]].

figures.label: long-term debt and lease obligations due after the next 12 months

statements.text: Its business brought in $7.4 billion of cash in the year ended December 31, 2025 and spent $2.1 billion on [[capital-expenditure|buildings and equipment]], leaving $5.3 billion of [[free-cash-flow|free cash flow]]: money it could use for dividends, buybacks, paying down debt or growing.
Free cash flow was smaller than its [[net-income|net income]] ($13.1 billion) that year, meaning less of its accounting profit turned into spare cash.

In the year ended December 31, 2025, the company spent $746 million buying back its own shares ([[share-buyback|buybacks]]), paid $8.8 billion in [[dividend|dividends]] to shareholders and invested $2.1 billion in buildings and equipment.
It earned about $46 of profit for every $100 of [[shareholders-equity|shareholders' equity]] in the year ended December 31, 2025. This is its [[return-on-equity|return on equity]] (46%).
[[eps|Earnings per share]] (diluted) rose 23.6% to $3.04 in the year ended December 31, 2025.
Over the 5 years to December 31, 2025, its [[operating-margin|operating margin]] rose to 28.7%, from 26.7%.
In the year to December 2025, it made $47.9 billion in [[revenue|sales]], 1.9% more than the year before. Sales in its latest three months (to April 2026) were up 12.1% on a year earlier.
In the year to December 2025, it kept $13.1 billion as [[net-income|profit]] after paying all its costs and taxes: about $27 of every $100 it made in sales, its [[profit-margin|profit margin]].

On April 3, 2026, for every $1 of bills due within a year, it had about $1.36 in cash and other things it expected to turn into cash in that time: more than enough to cover them. This is its [[current-ratio|current ratio]].
On April 3, 2026, it owed $39.1 billion in [[long-term-debt|loans and bonds]] not due for repayment within a year and held $10.6 billion in [[cash-and-equivalents|cash]].

statements.text: In the year to December 2025, its everyday business brought in $7.4 billion in [[cash-from-operations|cash]]. After paying for [[capital-expenditure|new buildings and equipment]], $5.3 billion was [[free-cash-flow|left over]].

In the year to December 2025, its biggest uses of money were: paying [[dividend|dividends]] to shareholders: $8.8 billion; [[capital-expenditure|new buildings and equipment]]: $2.1 billion; and [[share-buyback|buying back its own shares]]: $746 million.

wikipedia.title: The Coca-Cola Company
wikipedia.extract: The Coca-Cola Company is an American multinational corporation founded in January 1892, headquartered in Atlanta, Georgia. It manufactures, sells and markets soft drinks including Coca-Cola, other non-alcoholic beverage concentrates and syrups, and alcoholic beverages. Its stock is listed on the New York Stock Exchange and is a component of the DJIA and the S&P 500 and S&P 100 indices.
